newsitem.title: CHINA: China sentences corrupt official to 15 years.
newsitem.headline: China sentences corrupt official to 15 years.

text.p: A Chinese court has sentenced a senior Beijing city legislative official to 15 years in prison for taking bribes, the latest victim of a campaign to stamp out corruption among officials, state media said on Friday.

The Beijing Higher People's Court recently convicted Tie Ying, former deputy secretary of the Leading Communist Party Group of the Beijing Municipal People's Congress and a vice-chairwoman of the congress, of taking bribes, the Beijing Daily said.
Tie was jailed for 15 years for accepting 430,000 yuan ($51,000) in bribes between 1992 and 1995, some from a Hong Kong executive, the court said.
Earlier reports said Tie gave preferential treatment to the executive, allowing her benefactor to manage several municipal government projects in the form of a joint venture.
Another Beijing municipal official, Huang Jicheng, was sentenced to 10 years for taking bribes valued at 220,000 yuan, the newspaper said.
Court officials declined to comment on the cases.

Chinese disciplinary officials have been investigating corruption throughout the municipal administration since Vice Mayor Wang Baosen committed suicide on a suburban hillside in 1995 after coming under investigation in a $37 million graft scandal.
The scandal resulted in the fall in mid-1995 of Beijing city Communist Party boss Chen Xitong, who was also purged from the party's powerful Politburo.
Chen has yet to face charges and city officials have said he is unlikely to be indicted for a criminal offence although he could face disciplinary punishment for dereliction of duty.
Party chief Jiang Zemin has warned that corruption, which has surged in recent years with the deepening of economic reform, is the greatest threat to the survival of the ruling party.
